players.comment: James (back injury management) won't be available for Saturday's game against the Rockets, according to Kris Rhim of ESPN. James will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set after impressing in Friday's win over the Pacers, tallying 21 points (8-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and a block over 27 minutes. Dean Wade (hamstring) is questionable, while Joel Embiid (foot) and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) are out, so the 76ers will be depleted Saturday. Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe will have bigger roles on offense, while Jabari Walker, Dominick Barlow and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope will all see more minutes with James on the shelf.

McCollum (calf) will miss at least four weeks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network. The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.
Clarkson (foot) is out for Friday's game against the Heat. Plantar fasciitis is costing Clarkson a fifth consecutive contest Friday. His next chance to suit up arrives Sunday against the Hawks.

McConnell (hamstring) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the 76ers, Alex Golden of SI.com reports. McConnell will miss a third consecutive game Friday as he continues to manage a sore left hamstring. His next chance to return will come Saturday in the second leg of this back-to-back set; meanwhile, Quenton Jackson should continue to pick up additional minutes off the bench.

Prince underwent arthroscopic right knee surgery Nov. 18 and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports. Prince last appeared in a game for Detroit on Nov. 14 and is now set to miss an extended period as he recovers from knee surgery. However, the veteran forward's absence shouldn't significantly impact Detroit's rotation.

Grant was diagnosed with a grade 1 left calf strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks. Grant suffered the injury during Thursday's 126-98 victory over Golden State. He will now be sidelined for at least two weeks, with the team expected to provide an update on his condition at that time. While Grant is on the shelf, Taylor Hendricks and Kris Murray are candidates for more minutes.

Embiid has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Rockets due to right foot plantar fasciitis management, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports. Embiid missed two games due to an illness before returning to the floor Friday to face the Pacers, but he is now in line for yet another absence to close out this back-to-back set. Jaylen Brown (hamstring) and LeBron James (back) have also been ruled out for Saturday's contest, leaving Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe as the team's top remaining scoring options.

LaVine (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game versus the Warriors. LaVine will miss his second game of the 2026-27 campaign. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Timberwolves. In the meantime, Leaky Black, Emanuel Sharp and Malik Monk are candidates for more minutes, with one of those players expected to move into the starting lineup.

Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball. Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

players.comment: Martin didn't return for the second half of Friday's win over the Suns due to a left ankle sprain, Grant Afseth of DallasHoopsJournal.com reports. Martin finished the game with five points (2-6 FG, 1-5 3Pt), three rebounds, four assists and a steal across 14 minutes. Further tests will be needed to determine the severity of the injury, but Martin should be considered questionable to face the Celtics on Monday.

Landale (hip) is out for Friday's game against the Celtics. Landale won't suit up Friday and this will be his fifth consecutive absence. His next chance to play will come against the Knicks on Sunday.

Wagner (knee) won't be available for Friday's game against Toronto. Wagner suffered an injury Wednesday against the Bucks and won't be an option Friday. His status for the second leg of the back-to-back set Saturday at Charlotte is uncertain.

Robinson (quadriceps) is out for Friday's game against the Bucks. Robinson is carrying a day-to-day tag due to a left quadriceps strain, but the veteran sharpshooter is not ready to play yet and will miss a sixth consecutive game Friday. This means Kevin Huerter will likely continue seeing increased playing time for as long as Robinson is sidelined.

Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports. Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis. This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

Wade (hamstring) is out for Friday's game against the Pacers, Austin Krell of Vertical 76 reports. Wade was added to the injury report earlier Friday due to injury management of a hamstring problem, and in the end, the forward has been ruled out. This poses a problem for the 76ers, as Jaylen Brown (hamstring) is out as well. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope could be in line for a bigger role because of the absences. Wade's next chance to play will come Saturday against the Rockets on the second leg of a back-to-back set.

Brown (hamstring) underwent an MRI that showed no signs of a new injury or re-aggravation, but he didn't travel with the team for the road trip, so he will miss the team's next two games, Kris Rhim of ESPN reports. Brown's absence from the road trip means he won't play against the Pacers on Friday or against the Rockets on Saturday. However, the star forward might be able to return for Tuesday's matchup against the Grizzlies. With Brown out, Dean Wade (hamstring), Jabari Walker and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope are all options to see more playing time at small forward.

DiVincenzo (Achilles) has been cleared for team basketball activities and is targeting a return to game action in January, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports. DiVincenzo suffered a ruptured right Achilles in late April but is seemingly ahead of schedule in his recovery. With the veteran guard and Anthony Edwards (knee) both sidelined, Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon figure to continue seeing increased playing time.

Anunoby (calf) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Heat. The forward was previously listed as doubtful and will miss his third consecutive contest due to a left calf strain. Landry Shamet could remain in the starting lineup, while Josh Hart may absorb additional responsibilities on the wing. Anunoby's return to on-court activities is encouraging, but his next opportunity to play comes Sunday against Atlanta.

Curry (abdomen/oblique) has been ruled out for each of the Warriors' next three games, Anthony Slater of ESPN.com reports Curry has already missed each of Golden State's last six contests after suffering an oblique abdominal tear Nov. 11, and he won't be given the green light to return anytime in the immediate future. De'Anthony Melton is expected to continue working as the Warriors' starting point guard in the meantime, with LJ Cryer and Brandon Williams also getting more minutes.

Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

Bamba (illness) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Nuggets. Bamba will officially sit out Friday's contest after waking up feeling under the weather. Jaxson Hayes (knee) and Jusuf Nurkic (foot) are both available to face Denver and figure to absorb Bamba's playing time.

Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports. Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

Robinson has been ruled out Marc D'Amico of the Celtics' official sitefor Friday's game. Neemias Queta should continue handling the bulk of Boston's center minutes, with Luka Garza and Chris Cenac potentially receiving additional opportunities. Robinson's next chance to return comes Sunday against the Spurs.

Barrett has been diagnosed with a right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. Based on his re-evaluation timeline, Barrett likely won't return to game action until mid-December at the earliest. Jamison Battle, Allen Graves and Jamal Shead are candidates for increased playing time in Barrett's absence, especially while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is also sidelined.

Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic. It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

Haliburton (hamstring) has been ruled out per Scott Agness of FieldhouseFiles.com for Friday's game against the 76ers. The guard participated in practice activities earlier this week as he continues working toward his return. Haliburton's return to practice is encouraging, but Indiana continues exercising caution with his hamstring injury. He is still expected to have his return in mid-December.

players.comment: Pippen (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers. Pippen hasn't been available for Memphis since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a clear timeline to return. He can be deemed week-to-week going forward, though his absence could extend into mid-December if the Grizzlies don't advance in the NBA Cup.

McBride (groin) is out for Friday's game against the Heat. Friday marks a third straight absence for McBride. With the Knicks' backcourt a bit dinged up, Jose Alvarado could see enough playing time to warrant streaming attention in deeper fantasy setups.

Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days. Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

Cunningham (knee) is out for Friday's game against the Bucks. Cunningham won't suit up Friday and will miss a second straight game, and the third of his last five, while dealing with right knee tendinopathy. This means Daniss Jenkins should run the point for Detroit on Friday, while Isaiah Joe could be in line for another start at shooting guard. Cunningham's next chance to return will come Sunday against the Magic.

Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports. Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks. Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bucks, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports. Bittle continues to work his way back from a fractured right foot, as he's yet to make his 2026-27 season debut. He remains week-to-week until Toronto provides a definitive update.

Stewart (hip) is out for Friday's game against the Timberwolves, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports. Stewart was added to the injury report Friday, and the big man won't be suiting up.  This creates a problem for the Grizzlies, as they're also at risk of being without Zach Edey (ankle), which would give Taylor Hendricks a bigger role on offense.

Ball (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Grizzlies. The guard was previously questionable after spraining his left ankle during Wednesday's win over Oklahoma City. With Ball and Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined, Ayo Dosunmu and Bones Hyland should handle increased ball-handling responsibilities. Minnesota's depleted backcourt could also create additional scoring opportunities for Jaden McDaniels. Ball's next opportunity to return comes Monday against Sacramento.

Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

Detroit recalled Duren (hamstring) from the G League's Motor City Cruise on Wednesday. Duren has been dealing with a hamstring strain since October, and his return is not yet expected in immediate contests. The fact that he has practiced with the G League club is still a good sign as he makes progress in his recovery. Duren would be a reliable source of production once he's healthy, but until then, John Collins and Paul Reed may continue to absorb his responsibilities at center.

players.comment: Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced. Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

Mathurin (foot) is out for Friday's game against the Clippers. Mathurin has been downgraded to out, which shouldn't surprise anyone since he's been dealing with plantar fasciitis for quite some time. This will be his seventh consecutive absence.

Lively (foot) is out for Friday's game against the Suns. Lively has yet to suit up this season after undergoing right foot surgery last December. Recent comments from head coach Dusty May indicate he is progressing in his recovery, but he will remain sidelined Friday.

Walter won't return to Friday's game against Brooklyn due to a right quad contusion, Josh Lewenberg of TSN.ca reports. Walter put up three points (0-6 FG, 0-5 3Pt, 3-4 FT), three rebounds and three assists over 24 minutes before being ruled out for the night. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Nuggets, though it's unclear if he'll be ready to play by then.

Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

Youngblood (heel) is out for Friday's game against the Warriors. Youngblood is in line for a ninth straight absence due to a bone bruise in his right foot. His next opportunity to run the floor will arrive Sunday against the Pelicans.

Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

Newell underwent surgery Tuesday for a plantar plate tear in his left great toe, and he will be re-evaluated in approximately four months, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

Raynaud (knee) was recalled from the G League's Stockton Kings on Wednesday, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports. Raynaud presumably joined the G League Kings for practice Wednesday. He's recovering from a right patellar subluxation and remains without a timetable to return, and while it's encouraging that he's getting reps with Stockton, the big man can be considered week-to-week until the Kings offer another update on his status.

Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN. It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

Santos exited Friday's game against the Trail Blazers with a knee injury in the second half and won't return. Santos lasted just eight minutes in the game, posting five points (2-4 FG, 1-1 3Pt), two rebounds and a steal while coming off the bench. Further tests will be needed to determine the severity of the injury, but for the time being, he should be considered questionable to face the Clippers on Sunday.

Boozer (ankle) will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. The rookie standout has been diagnosed with a moderate-grade ankle sprain, and he'll be sidelined for at least the next month or so. It's a tough blow for an upstart Grizzlies team, which will now rely even more heavily on Ty Jerome's playmaking for the foreseeable future. Taylor Hendricks has a chance to nail down a consistent role off the bench as well.

Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports. The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months. Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday. Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.
Lawal (groin) is out for Friday's game against the Suns. Lawal will miss a fifth straight game due to a right groin strain. His next opportunity to suit up comes Monday against the Celtics.

Tomlin (back) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies. Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

Niederhauser suffered a right toe injury during Friday's game against the Pelicans and won't return, Joey Linn of SI.com reports. Niederhauser suffered the injury on the same foot he previously had surgery on, so it's clear the Clippers are being overly cautious. The big man finished the game with two points (1-3 FG, 0-1 FT) and a block in 10 minutes off the bench. The Clippers play again Sunday on the road against the Warriors.

Biberovic (heel) is out for Friday's game against the Suns. Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and he doesn't have a clear return date. He should be considered week-to-week until the Mavs offer an update about his recovery.

Jakucionis (ankle) won't play Friday's game against the Pistons. Jakucionis will miss his second game of the season due to left ankle tenosynovitis. In his absence, Ryan Rollins, Caris LeVert and AJ Green could see expanded roles, while rookie Brayden Burries should also get a slight bump in minutes.

players.comment: The Pistons announced Tuesday that Okorie (oblique) will miss at least two weeks, per Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com. Okorie has been diagnosed with an oblique strain, which he sustained in a G League game. The rookie first-rounder has logged a grand total of 20 minutes across five brief appearances, so his absence doesn't have major fantasy ramifications.

De Larrea (knee) is out for Friday's game against the Suns. De Larrea continues to miss time with a right knee strain, and it's not clear at this time where he's at in his rehab. He can be considered week-to-week until further notice.

Traore will be re-evaluated in approximately 8-10 weeks due to a right hamstring strain, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports. Traore had a productive start to his second year in the NBA, though he's now set to miss an extended period after sustaining a hamstring injury in Friday's loss to Orlando. With the 20-year-old point guard sidelined, Egor Demin, Mikel Brown and Keon Ellis are candidates for increased playing time.

Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports. Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio. Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

Irving (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Suns, Noah Weber of TheSmokingCuban.com reports. The Mavericks will give Irving a breather to manage his surgically repaired left knee. His absence will likely open up more playmaking opportunities for Cooper Flagg; meanwhile, Max Christie and Naji Marshall are likely to receive a bump in playing time.

Leonard has begun individual on-court workouts following treatment to address swelling in his left knee, and he will be re-evaluated in one week, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports. Leonard continues to progress in his recovery, and the Raptors are expected to provide another update in a week. Collin Murray-Boyles and Allen Graves will likely continue seeing increased burn for as long as Leonard is sidelined.

Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports. Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

Drummond (concussion) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Heat. Drummond played just nine minutes prior to exiting Wednesday's 121-102 win over Cleveland due to a concussion. Mohamed Diawara and James Wiseman will likely get a boost in playing time off the Knicks' bench with Drummond sidelined. His next chance to suit up will come against the Hawks on Sunday.

Lillard (calf) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Warriors. The veteran guard is dealing with right calf tightness and soreness. Lillard's absence creates additional ball-handling and scoring opportunities for Jrue Holiday and Deni Avdija, while Scoot Henderson could see increased playing time. Lillard's next opportunity to return comes Sunday against New Orleans.

The Pelicans transferred Reese from the G League's Laketown Squadron, and he will be available for New Orleans' game against the Warriors on Monday. Reese dropped a 15-point, 15-rebound double-double in the Squadron's win over the Mexico City Capitanes on Saturday and will return to the parent club ahead of its game Monday. Through five regular-season appearances at the NBA level this season, the big man is averaging 1.2 points and 1.0 rebounds in 5.4 minutes per tilt.
